research_mode: official Ministry of Justice and HMPPS accredited statistics; fail-closed limitations; no parcel score, candidate value or business result

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: Female remand and sentenced self-harm rates
verified_claims: In the female estate, the 2025 self-harm rate was 6,172 per 1,000 remand prisoners and 5,447 per 1,000 sentenced prisoners.
limitations: Institutional custody-status rates are not suitable for residential or parcel comparisons.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: Overall remand and sentenced rates
verified_claims: Across the prison estate, the self-harm rate was 849 per 1,000 remand prisoners and 804 per 1,000 sentenced prisoners in 2025.
limitations: These rates use prison-population denominators and cannot be assigned to a geographic parcel.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: IPP and recalled-prisoner rates
verified_claims: Within sentenced prisoners, the 2025 self-harm rate was 1,290 per 1,000 for IPP prisoners and 1,366 per 1,000 for recalled prisoners.
limitations: Sentence-status subgroups have distinctive risk profiles and provide no parcel-level signal.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: Self-harm methods
verified_claims: Cutting or scratching was involved in 53% of self-harm incidents in 2025, while self-strangulation was involved in 26%.
limitations: Method shares are sensitive custodial-health statistics and do not describe external public-space hazards.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: Cutting or scratching by estate sex
verified_claims: Cutting or scratching featured in 60% of male-estate and 33% of female-estate self-harm incidents in 2025.
limitations: Estate differences cannot be extrapolated to residents or locations outside custody.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: Self-harm location
verified_claims: Cells and common areas accounted for 72% of male-estate and 81% of female-estate self-harm incidents in 2025.
limitations: Prison internal locations have no valid spatial equivalence to land parcels or neighbourhood public spaces.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: First 30 days in current prison
verified_claims: Twenty-one percent of self-harm incidents occurred within the first 30 days in the current prison.
limitations: Time-since-transfer exposure is an institutional factor and cannot be converted into geographic risk.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: Repeated self-harm by sex
verified_claims: In 2025, 53% of males and 59% of females who self-harmed did so more than once during the year.
limitations: Repeated-event proportions do not indicate the number or safety of geographic locations.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: Younger-age self-harm rates
verified_claims: The highest 2025 self-harm incident rates were among prisoners aged 18 to 20 at 1,760 per 1,000, 21 to 24 at 1,355, and 25 to 29 at 1,176.
limitations: Age-specific prison rates cannot be applied to the age profile of a neighbourhood or property.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: Prison population annual change
verified_claims: The prison population on 31 March 2026 was around 600 people, or 0.7%, lower than at the end of March 2025.
limitations: Population change affects institutional rates but is not evidence about any parcel.
